source_name: ČNB – Supervision of payment institutions and e-money institutions (EN)
why_relevant: English-language statement of supervisory scope over payment institutions, EMIs, small-scale payment service providers and small-scale e-money issuers — the category ontology needed to interpret the Czech register and to map CZ categories onto EU (PSD2/EBA) equivalents.

source_name: ČNB – Financial Market Supervision Report (annual, CS/EN)
why_relevant: Annual narrative on licensing activity, enforcement, sanctions and structural change in the CZ banking and payments sector. Aggregates entrant/exit counts and supervisory priorities — context for why particular institutions appear or vanish from public tenders.

source_name: ČNB – Seznamy institucí pro potřeby měnové a finanční statistiky
why_relevant: Statistical institution lists (MFIs etc.) provide a second, differently-maintained identifier set for CZ banks and financial institutions — useful for entity resolution when matching tender bidders to licensed entities.

source_name: ÚOOÚ – ukončené kontroly (completed inspections), banking and financial sector
why_relevant: Inspection reports naming specific banks (UniCredit Bank CZ&SK, GE Money Bank) and citing the payments act (zák. č. 370/2017 Sb. o platebním styku). They reveal which data-processing and client-communication technologies banks actually run, and compliance failures that trigger remediation procurement in security/IT.

source_name: ÚOOÚ – povinně zveřejňované informace / poskytnuté informace (FOI disclosures)
why_relevant: FOI-released inspection protocols and information on administrative proceedings in the banking and financial sector contain operational detail (systems, vendors, processes) that is not in the summarised public reports.

source_name: MF ČR – Metodický pokyn CHJ č. 3 (Metodika veřejného nakupování) a metodické materiály
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance central-harmonisation-unit guidance on public buying (3E principles), updated in v2.0 (Dec 2024) in line with the National Public Procurement Strategy 2024–2028. It sets the evaluation logic contracting authorities are told to apply — i.e. how a banking-services or payment-terminal bid will actually be judged.

source_name: Státní pokladna (MF) – metodické informace / CSÚIS
why_relevant: The State Treasury programme is itself a large, continuously procured payment/accounting IT estate (CSÚIS, IISSP). Its methodological bulletins signal system changes, interface obligations on public bodies, and hence upcoming integration and payment-infrastructure contracts.

source_name: ISVZ / NIPEZ – Informační systém o veřejných zakázkách (open data & dashboards)
source_subtype: statutory procurement information system / open data
why_relevant: The statutory procurement information system (§224 zák. č. 134/2016 Sb.) publishes market datasets, dashboards and OpenData. It is the structural backbone against which regulator-side signals (ÚOHS decisions, NKÚ audits) can be joined to actual notices and awards.

source_name: Wolters Kluwer ASPI – Expertní databáze rozhodnutí ÚOHS ve věci veřejných zakázek
why_relevant: Commercial, editorially enriched database of ÚOHS procurement decisions with legal tagging and cross-references to case law — valuable for precision retrieval of banking-services precedent, but paywalled.

source_name: Portál o veřejných zakázkách – Individuální elektronické nástroje (certified e-tendering tool register)
why_relevant: Official MMR-maintained list of all certified individual electronic tools (elektronické nástroje) usable for e-tendering in CZ, with operator names and tool URLs. This is the master index that enumerates every commercial platform in this cell in one page — E-ZAK/X-EN (QCM), Tenderarena (Tendersystems), Josephine (NAR Marketing/Sentinet), PROEBIZ profily, zadavatel.cz/e-zakazky (OTIDEA), CENT (Osigeno), KDV, eCentre, FirstBuySale (ANETE), x:tendr (RTS), Eveza (NWT), Athena/nasprofil (GC Logix), eZakazky (YOUR SYSTEM), PARC (PXE), plus special-purpose tools.

source_name: E-ZAK (QCM s.r.o.) – e-tendering platform, multi-tenant buyer profiles
why_relevant: One of the two dominant CZ e-tendering engines; deployed as per-buyer subdomains (e.g. mfcr.ezak.cz, ezak.cnb.cz) and a shared instance ezak.e-tenders.cz. Indexing the E-ZAK deployment pattern gives access to thousands of buyer profiles including financial-sector public bodies. QCM (with PVU + Gemin) claims ~42-43% of all registered CZ contracting authorities.

source_name: E-ZAK ČNB – Czech National Bank buyer profile
why_relevant: The central bank's own E-ZAK instance — the single highest-value banking-sector buyer profile in CZ for IT, cash-handling, payments and security procurement. Confirms the platform-to-buyer mapping thesis of this cell (ČNB also has a Gemin profile and a PVU profile page).

source_name: Tender arena (Tendersystems s.r.o.)
why_relevant: Certified e-tendering tool with a large share of CZ buyer profiles (~2,800 profiles / ~11% per third-party analysis). Supports full ZZVZ procedures, buyer-profile publication, e-bids and e-auctions; its public tender board indexes many buyers at once.

source_name: JOSEPHINE (NAR marketing / Sentinet, PROEBIZ family)
why_relevant: Cross-border CZ/SK e-tendering platform with a single public tender list covering all buyers using it — a compact multi-buyer index. Strong in SK and growing in CZ; the same vendor family also serves corporate (non-public) purchasing, so private-sector bank RFPs can surface here.

source_name: PROEBIZ – profily zadavatelů / TENDERBOX
source_subtype: commercial e-tendering / e-auction vendor + profile host
why_relevant: PROEBIZ's buyer-profile hosting and TENDERBOX e-tendering/e-auction suite. Directly relevant because PROEBIZ explicitly serves corporate purchasing as well as public procurement — the most likely route to private-sector (incl. bank/fintech) RFPs run on the same tooling.

source_name: profilzadavatele.cz
why_relevant: Another high-volume buyer-profile hosting tool (cited ~5,600-5,800 profiles, ~20% share in third-party market analyses). Acts as a noticeboard aggregating many buyers' calls and tender documentation in one domain.

source_name: zadavatel.cz / e-zakazky.cz (OTIDEA CZ s.r.o.)
why_relevant: Certified OTIDEA tool pair (~2,380 profiles, ~8% share) — zadavatel.cz is the buyer-profile front end, e-zakazky.cz the procedural workspace. Another sizeable slice of the buyer-profile universe not covered by QCM or Tendersystems.

source_name: Národní elektronický nástroj (NEN) / NIPEZ
why_relevant: State-run e-tendering tool and the reference point against which commercial platform market share is measured; also carries a searchable buyer-profile registry that resolves which commercial platform a given buyer actually uses. Essential cross-reference layer for this cell even though it is not commercial.

source_name: Datlab s.r.o. – TenderMan / Kontrola / Sankce (commercial procurement data & alerts)
why_relevant: The leading CZ commercial procurement-data house: aggregates VVZ notices, all buyer profiles and the contracts register into a supplier/buyer analytics product (TenderMan, cited ~550k contracts from VVZ+profiles, ~3m register contracts, ~200k suppliers) plus register-of-contracts watchdog alerting. A paid mirror that resolves the fragmentation across the platforms above.

source_name: TenderMonitor.cz – subscription tender alerting
why_relevant: Paid alert service covering Czech and EU tenders with fixed-fee subscription; a low-effort way to get push notification of banking/payments CPV activity across platforms without building crawlers.

source_name: dZakazky.cz – supplier-side tender search and e-mail watchdog
why_relevant: Supplier-facing aggregator of above- and below-threshold municipal and other public tenders with a trial e-mail watchdog; another commercial mirror useful for cross-checking coverage gaps of the big platforms.

source_name: Opentender.eu – Czech Republic portal (DIGIWHIST)
why_relevant: Open-data mirror of CZ (and 34 other jurisdictions') procurement data built from TED plus national portals, with per-authority and per-supplier pages and bulk downloads. Best free CEE-wide comparative mirror; code is open on GitHub (okfde/opentender.eu).

source_name: Elektronizace-zakazek.cz – market-share analytics of CZ e-tendering tools
why_relevant: Periodic published statistics on how many buyer profiles each electronic tool hosts (PVU, E-ZAK, Tender arena, NEN, profilzadavatele.cz, OTIDEA...). The single best source for prioritising which platforms to crawl first and for detecting migrations between tools.

source_name: International commercial tender aggregators covering CZ (Tendersinfo, BidDetail, TenderImpulse, Jorpex)
why_relevant: Paid English-language mirrors of CZ tenders. Low unique value (they re-publish VVZ/TED) but useful as an English-language cross-check and for cross-border comparison; Jorpex publishes a country guide naming the underlying CZ sources.

source_name: Komerční banka – supplier information page (private-sector buyer entry point)
why_relevant: Example of the private-sector side of this cell: a major CZ bank publishes supplier terms and codes of conduct but — as fetched — names no e-sourcing platform. Confirms that commercial-bank sourcing in CZ is largely invitation-only and not visible on the public e-tendering platforms.

source_name: MPSV / Úřad práce ČR – Jednotný portál, evidence volných pracovních míst
why_relevant: Statutory national vacancy register: employers (including banks and their IT/procurement units) must notify vacancies to Úřad práce. Gives an official, structured, non-paywalled stream of hiring signals (e.g. 'projektový manažer migrace', 'manažer dodavatelů', 'karetní systémy') that precede a formal tender by 6-18 months.
